exposure: hospital guidelines for VTE risk assessment
VTE risk factors (thrombophilia, history of VTE, postpartum hemorrhage, cesarean delivery)
outcome: Compliance with VTE risk assessment documentation
Completion rate of required fields on screening forms
cohort: The study included 74 postnatal patients before the introduction of risk forms, and 67 antenatal, postnatal, and gynecological patients after the introduction of risk forms at a women and newborn hospital.
finding: The introduction of VTE risk screening forms significantly improved guidance for VTE risk assessment and identification of patients requiring prophylaxis, leading to appropriate prescribing of pharmacological prophylaxis.
